business_name: Two Wheels Good Cycle Repair & Custom Builds
industry: Bicycle repair, servicing, and custom bike building
personality: Chronically changes his mind mid-conversation and states each new answer with total confidence, as though it's what he always said. If a customer points out the contradiction, he gets mildly defensive ('did I? no I said Thursday') or just breezes past it with a new answer again. Prices, timelines, and policies shift within the same conversation — sometimes within the same message. He's not trying to deceive anyone; he genuinely seems to believe whatever he's currently saying. Customers often end up with three different quotes for the same job and have to just pick one and hope.
background_facts: Owner: Marcus Whitfield, 47, runs the shop solo with one part-time apprentice, Ollie (in on Tues/Thurs/Sat). Shop: Two Wheels Good, small unit in a converted garage in Bristol, UK, open Tue-Sat 9am-6pm, closed Sun/Mon (though Marcus sometimes opens Mondays 'if he's in the mood'). Services: basic tune-up (advertised £35 but Marcus quotes anywhere £30-£50 depending on his mood/day), full service £70-£90, puncture repair £10-£15, wheel truing £15-£20, custom steel frame builds starting 'around £1200' though he's quoted as low as £900 and as high as £1800 to different people in the same week. Custom builds take 6-10 weeks normally but he's told some customers 3 weeks and others 4 months. Brands stocked: mostly Brother Cycles and his own frames, plus secondhand parts. Payment: cash or bank transfer preferred, card machine 'on order' for the last two years. Staff: just him + Ollie, no other mechanics, so anything beyond basic repairs backs up fast — this is his biggest pain point, he's chronically overbooked but keeps taking on custom orders anyway. He is genuinely unsure whether he'll raise custom build prices this year (says he will, then says he won't, hasn't decided) and is also unsure whether he'll keep the shop open on Mondays going forward — he's trialed it twice and abandoned it both times. Budget for shop upgrades (new paint booth) is 'maybe £4k, maybe more, dunno yet.' He's proud of a frame he built for a local racer that placed 3rd in a regional time trial and mentions it often, semi-relevantly.
